Subject: A correction to the takings and GST template (v1.0 to v1.2)

A correction to the takings and GST template

I got the GST formula wrong in the versions I put up between 12 August and 1 October, and I know some of you have already filed with the sheet. That is on me, and I would rather explain it properly than leave it buried in a comment.

Ravi Subramaniam spotted it first on his own takings, and Shu Fen (Numbers For Hawkers) confirmed it independently and pushed me to write this up. Thank you both. Melvin Ong's reply in the same thread is fair as well. People trusted the sheet partly because I put my name to it and I am an accountant, so you were entitled to expect the numbers to hold.

What was wrong

In v1.0 to v1.2, column F multiplied whatever you keyed in by 9%. That is right only when the amounts you enter exclude GST. If you key in GST-inclusive takings — what you actually collected from customers, including the GST — the GST portion is 9/109 of that figure, not 9% of it.

Ravi's example: takings of $1,090, GST inclusive, showed GST of $98.10. The correct GST is $90. The template was overstating it by $8.10 on that day, and the old result was 1.09 times what it should have been.

Who is affected

Only if you key in GST-inclusive takings, which is most hawkers. If your entries exclude GST, your figures were right and nothing changes for you.

The affected versions are v1.0, v1.1 and v1.2. The fix is in v1.3, uploaded on 8 November, with the changelog alongside the download link below. There have been 412 downloads since 12 August, so please do not assume you were unaffected.

One thing to get right in v1.3: the new setting in H2 has to match the amounts you actually entered. Choose "prices exclude GST" only for entries that exclude GST. If your receipts include GST — even if your menu prices do not show GST — use the inclusive setting. Setting it the wrong way is what caused the problem in the first place.

Why I missed it

I tested v1.0 against my own sample figures, and my samples were already ex-GST, so the check passed and I saw nothing wrong. That was my error and I am not going to dress it up.

What this means for your GST

The mistake pushes the GST figure up, not down. Nobody has underpaid IRAS because of this. If anything, some of you may have overpaid, and that is worth checking.

If you already filed with the sheet

The first step is to download v1.3 and set the toggle to match your entries.

The second is to re-key your takings for the quarter and compare the GST figure against the one on your F5. Only Box 6 was affected — the sales total in Box 1 was worked out separately and was correct in every version.

The third, if the two figures differ, is to find out what happens next. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error like this goes into a later F5 or needs a GST F7, and I am not going to restate them here and get it wrong. Please check IRAS's errors and corrections page, and speak to your filer if you have one. Please do not amend your records until you know which route applies.

If you have not filed yet, use v1.3 and you can ignore the rest of this.

Download link below (v1.3, uploaded 8 Nov 2026), changelog alongside. Do leave a comment if anything is still unclear.
